_comment: fontScaling / maxFontScale (ticket sjui-label-font-size-ignores-dynamic-type, ruling 2026-11-13): the size a component's text is drawn at. Every face's runtime reads these; shared/core/font_scale_rule.py is the rule in Python, pinned against them by jui_tools/tests/test_font_scale_vectors.py.

rule.follows: A text follows the OS / browser text size when its fontScaling says so; absent, the app default (Configuration font scaling), which is true unless the app sets it.
rule.drawn: Not following: the declared fontSize at every text size (iOS pins the component to the standard size, Android reads fontSize as dp, the web as px). Following: fontSize x scale, where scale is what the system multiplies this size by (Android 14+: non-linear, the factor its conversion gives for this size; iOS and the web: one factor for every size); with maxFontScale, at most fontSize x maxFontScale.
rule.partial: partialAttributes' sizes follow their component's declaration.
rule.noFontSize: A component that declares fontScaling or maxFontScale but no fontSize takes the size it draws without one as its fontSize, so the declaration has a size to keep or cap (ruling 2026-11-13). That size per face: iOS Label and Button SwiftJsonUIConfiguration font.size (17 unless the app sets it), TextView, SelectBox and IconLabel their own default 16, TextField, CheckBox, Radio and Switch font.size (17, SwiftUI's .body at the standard size); Android the current text style's size (Material3 bodyLarge, 16sp unless the theme changes it), TextField and TextView Configuration.TextField.defaultFontSize (14); the web 16px, Segment 14px. A component that declares neither keeps the face's own default font, as before. On iOS a text that writes no font attribute at all, in an app with no fontProvider, sets no font: it keeps the environment's text style (.body, lines 22 high) and grows as .body does, by the text style's own table — 17, 19, 21, 23, 28, 33, 40, 47, 53 pt from large to accessibility5, not 17 × the ratios above — with the declaration reaching it through the Dynamic Type size .body reads: the system's; under maxFontScale the largest step whose .body stays within 17 × maxFontScale (a 1.1 cap is the standard size, .body at xLarge being 19); the standard size when fontScaling is false. With a provider it is the provider's font at the size above (SwiftJsonUI 5d16684, the orchestrator's rulings 2026-11-14).
rule.letterSpacing: Letter spacing a face adds in an absolute unit (a theme's text style, as Android's Material letterSpacing in sp) is drawn by the same factor as the size: kept as given when the text does not follow (Android reads it as dp), at most spacing x maxFontScale when capped. Spacing relative to the size (em) follows the size and needs nothing. iOS adds none of its own (no letterSpacing attribute; the system font's tracking is a function of the size it is drawn at, which is already the rule's).
rule.iosCap: iOS caps by a Dynamic Type step: the largest step whose .body ratio (UIFontMetrics on the running OS) is at most maxFontScale; none: the largest step; below every step above the standard one: the standard step.

cases.name: a step's own ratio is that step

knownDifferences.where: iOS, a text with no font attribute in an app with no fontProvider
knownDifferences.difference: It is drawn by .body's own Dynamic Type table (19, 21, 23, 28, 33 … pt) where Android and the web draw 17 × the ratio (18.67, 20, 22.33, 26.33, 31 … at the same steps): the same size at the standard step, 5 to 10 % larger at the big ones. It keeps iOS's own .body there, as before the rule; maxFontScale still holds, by .body's table.
